narrative.overview:
ElegantClipboard’s UI is a precision desktop instrument: summoned, scanned, dismissed. Personality is restrained, slightly soft, and native-feeling — never loud. Density is high but orderly: history cards, metadata, and controls pack information without marketing chrome or decorative glass stacks.

The visual system is Chakra-inspired semantics projected onto GPUI Kit: one accent voice, cool zinc neutrals, light/dark parity, and optional OS materials (frosted / mica / opaque). Motion is short and state-bearing (150 / 200 / 300 ms Chakra curves). Global theme.shadow and theme.focus_ring stay off; depth and focus come from tonal fills, hairlines, and Kit’s thin control outlines.

Confirmed rejections: marketing hero/illustration bands; neon glassmorphism or heavy shadow piles; thick custom focus rings; browser-chrome metaphors (address bar / multi-tab app shell).
keyCharacteristics: GPUI Kit catalog controls only for catalog interactions
Material shell vs solid popover split
One accent family at a time (default 鸭青); neutrals stay zinc
Motion respects OS reduce-motion; feedback stays legible without spectacle

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: Only the active accent palette may color interactive emphasis (primary, selection, links, rings). Neutrals never compete with a second brand hue on the same screen.

rules.name: The Popover Is Solid Rule
rules.body: Dialogs, menus, notifications, floating action bars, and hover reading chrome use opaque popover/surface. Translucency belongs to the window shell and shared list wash — not to every floating layer.

rules.name: The Hairline Rule
rules.body: Under materials, shared separators use ~55% border alpha so they read as tonal cuts across the backdrop; controls that need a hard edge use emphasized/input, not a second border color family.

rules.name: The No Display Face Rule
rules.body: Do not introduce a decorative display font for chrome. Hierarchy is size and weight only inside the system UI family.

rules.name: The Metadata Whisper Rule
rules.body: Time, size, and source stay on secondary text at small size; they never steal accent color except when the row is selected.

rules.name: The Twelve-Pixel Gutter Rule
rules.body: Content left/right inset stays 12px unless a surface documents an exception (e.g. dialog internal padding).

rules.name: The Virtual List Rule
rules.body: Long history never switches to paginated page chrome; height virtualization is the density strategy.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: Cards and list rows do not carry drop shadows at rest. Selection is accent wash + ring stroke, not elevation.

rules.name: The Shell vs Chrome Rule
rules.body: Translucency is a window-material choice. Floating decision UI stays solid for legibility and shadow honesty.

rules.name: The Radius Is a Preference Rule
rules.body: Do not hard-code a one-off radius fashion per feature; read the theme radius tokens.

rules.name: The Window Chrome Is Native Rule
rules.body: App-drawn radii stop at controls and content; system window shape stays system.

dos: Do use GPUI Kit catalog components for buttons, inputs, dialogs, tabs, switches, checkboxes, settings chrome, notifications, virtual lists, and Kbd.
Do read colors from theme semantic tokens after design_system::apply — never local light/dark hex tables in features.
Do keep main-window chrome borderless with the grip + status bar pattern; settings may use Kit TitleBar.
Do honor reduce-motion: cut spatial travel, keep opacity/color state changes that encode feedback.
Do keep popovers/menus/dialogs on solid surfaces; put materials on the shell.
Do match pointer hover and keyboard focus to the same selected row model.
Do stay within the spacing scale (4–24) and control heights (28 / 32 / 36).
donts: Don't add a second component library or hand-roll a Kit equivalent control.
Don't enable thick global focus rings or decorative multi-stop neon gradients.
Don't put marketing heroes, illustrative empty-state mascots, or web app tab-strip chrome into the utility shell.
Don't silently degrade rich clipboard formats in UI copy affordances; errors for missing formats stay explicit.
Don't paint nested panels with independent glass stacks that fight DWM/AppKit blur.
Don't invent a display typeface or a second accent on the same view.
Don't use shadows on resting list cards to fake hierarchy — use density, type, and selection wash.
Don't claim iOS HIG / Material 3 mobile patterns; this system is desktop GPUI despite adaptive product platform tagging.
